stories.headline: Assam Cabinet Clears Defence Park, CBI Flood Probe, ₹2,440 Paddy Rate; Tightens Polygamy Rules
stories.title: Assam Cabinet Clears Defence Park, CBI Flood Probe, ₹2,440 Paddy Rate; Tightens Polygamy Rules
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
article_sentences: GUWAHATI: The Assam Cabinet has taken several crucial decisions pertaining to polygamy, defence park, ropeway, Zubeen Kshetra, CBI probe into the recent flashfood in Charaideo and Sivasagar, paddy procurement, etc.

Presided by Chief Minister Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma, the cabinet on Tuesday decided that departmental proceedings would be initiated against any government official found to have indulged in polygamy with proof, besides dismissing such officials and debarring them from any future government employment.
Civil Service Conduct Rules regarding the matter too received nod from the cabinet.

In order to enable Assam capture a slice of the growing defence production industry in the country, the cabinet also okayed handing over 6,000 bigha of land near Nellie in Morigaon district to the Industries & Commerce Department.
The land would be used for setting up a defence park where defence industries could be set up.
In another crucial move, the cabinet also gave nod to signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) by the Government of Assam with the Centre for ropeways.
A dedicated Ropeway Development Authority would be set up, where the Centre would hold 51% stake and the state government 49%.

Further, in addition to the ongoing ropeway project from Kamakhya railway station to Kamakhya temple atop Nilachal Hills, new ropeway projects would be taken up between Gangananagar and Bhubon Pahar in Barak Valley, Agnigarh Pahar and Bharavi Mandir in Sonitpur district, and at Jatinga in Dima Hasao district.
The cabinet also decided to hand over the probe into the flashfloods in Charaideo and Sivasagar districts earlier this year to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), and find the root cause.
Dispur will submit a request to the CBI within the next 10 days to take up the case.
Clearing land-related confusion regarding Zubeen Kshetra, the cabinet has given nod to regularising two bighas of land adjacent to the site after acquisition.
The private party owning the land has been given an alternative site.

stories.headline: US mid-terms may help D-Street break free from geopolitical overhang
stories.title: US mid-terms may help D-Street break free from geopolitical overhang
stories.summary: Mumbai: All eyes are on the US mid-term elections, with investors looking for signs on whether the outcome could ease global geopolitical uncertainties, a key factor for the outlook on equities.The elections will determine which party controls the House of Representatives and the Senate for the remaining two years of US President Donald Trump's term."The midterm outcome could influence Indian markets through trade policy, global investor sentiment and currency movements," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services. "If Trump loses control of Congress, greater scrutiny of his tariff policies could ease some trade concerns. If Republicans retain control, existing trade and immigration policies may continue, keeping uncertainty elevated." Initial results are expected in India early on Wednesday morning as polling stations close across US time zones.135516833135516837Historical data show that the Nifty has gained the most over one-, three- and six months after the US midterm elections.Of the seven mid-term polls since 1998, the Nifty has gained five times each in a month, three and six months.Read more: Sebi levies Rs 40 lakh penalty on four entities in Axis MF front-running caseMadhavi Arora, chief economist at Emkay Global Financial Services, said a Democratic-controlled Congress could constrain Trump through legislative checks, but he would retain substantial authority over tariffs, immigration and foreign policy."Fiscal policy is likely to remain expansionary under either outcome, putting a floor under US bond yields," she said. She cautioned that the Iran conflict could re-escalate after the midterms, irrespective of the outcome.Read more: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on WednesdayThe post-election policy direction will matter more than the election result itself, said Ankur Punj, managing director at Equirus Wealth. "Investors should avoid tactical allocation decisions based purely on the US political outcome and remain focused on domestic earnings growth, valuations and asset allocation. opening: Mumbai: All eyes are on the US mid-term elections, with investors looking for signs on whether the outcome could ease global geopolitical uncertainties, a key factor for the outlook on equities.

The elections will determine which party controls the House of Representatives and the Senate for the remaining two years of US President Donald Trump's term." The midterm outcome could influence Indian markets through trade policy, global investor sentiment and currency movements," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services.
body: "If Trump loses control of Congress, greater scrutiny of his tariff policies could ease some trade concerns.
Historical data show that the Nifty has gained the most over one-, three- and six months after the US midterm elections.
Of the seven mid-term polls since 1998, the Nifty has gained five times each in a month, three and six months.

Sebi levies Rs 40 lakh penalty on four entities in Axis MF front-running caseMadhavi Arora, chief economist at Emkay Global Financial Services, said a Democratic-controlled Congress could constrain Trump through legislative checks, but he would retain substantial authority over tariffs, immigration and foreign policy." Fiscal policy is likely to remain expansionary under either outcome, putting a floor under US bond yields," she said.
She cautioned that the Iran conflict could re-escalate after the midterms, irrespective of the outcome.
Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday.
The post-election policy direction will matter more than the election result itself, said Ankur Punj, managing director at Equirus Wealth.
"Investors should avoid tactical allocation decisions based purely on the US political outcome and remain focused on domestic earnings growth, valuations and asset allocation.
The real market drivers for India will be crude, US yields and FII flows," he said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asserts Right to Protest Must Not Lead to Indefinite Occupation of Public Spaces
stories.title: Supreme Court Asserts Right to Protest Must Not Lead to Indefinite Occupation of Public Spaces
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi, Nov 3: The Supreme Court on Tuesday orally observed that the right to protest cannot be exercised by occupying a designated protest site indefinitely, stressing that such places must be allotted for specified periods to ensure that other groups also get an opportunity to exercise their constitutional rights.

A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions arising from the October protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.
"You cannot occupy a site for all time to come.
There are other protesters.
Where will the farmers go?
Where will the workers go?
Where will the trade unions go?
Where will the homeless go?
Everybody has a right to protest," the apex court remarked.

It further observed that protest sites must be made available to different groups for designated periods, adding that no organisation could claim an exclusive right over a public space merely because it had occupied it first.
"There may be one site or two, but everybody has a right to protest.
You cannot exclude other people merely because you have occupied the site," the CJI-led Bench said.
